title: optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion, scheduling, KV-cache & continuous-batching
author: Ethan Rodriguez
description: Summary: This PR improves quantized inference kernel performance for INT8/FP8 models by combining smoothquant scaling, dequantization-fusion on the attention matmul path, and scheduler-level optimizations to better utilize KV-cache and continuous batching. Motivation: production workloads observed high per-token latency variance and suboptimal GPU utilization for mixed-precision quantized variants. These changes reduce token latency tail while maintaining or improving throughput and preserving numeric fidelity on internal evals. What changed: 1) Kernel changes: implemented fused dequant+gemm kernels for INT8->FP32/FP16 and FP8 fast-paths that apply smoothquant scaling pre-dequant to avoid an extra elementwise pass; added auto-vectorized microkernels for QKV projection on Ampere/Blackwell GPUs; improved shared-memory tiling to reduce global loads for sequence lengths > 512. 2) Scheduling: heuristic scheduler updates route short, latency-sensitive requests to low-batch, low-latency config (fast-path) while grouping long-generation requests into continuous-batching pipelines; new per-model profile table chooses kernel variant based on seq_len distribution and quant type. 3) KV-cache integrations: KV-cache now exposes compressed INT8 representations for warm prefixes and a fast dequant-on-read fast-path; cache misses trigger asynchronous pre-dequant work to overlap with decoding. 4) Batching heuristics: continuous-batching now prioritizes prefix cache reuse and aligns batch composition to power-of-two sequence lengths to improve memory reuse across warps. 5) Tests and evals: added microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf tests; added regression checks (numeric closeness thresholds) and stability tests across 8-bit/FP8 variants. Risks and mitigation: numeric drift under extreme inputs was detected in early prototypes - mitigated by dynamic scale clamping and post-fusion validation. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag; A/B test on dedicated clusters followed by hosted rollout if perf/regressions are within thresholds.

review_comments: Ava Chen (reviewer): Nice end-to-end work. Question: how is numerical stability across FP8 formats (E4M3 vs hybrid) validated? Can we add a tolerance table for each model family?

Ethan Rodriguez (author): Added per-model tolerance table in tests and dynamic clamp logic in kernels; see runtime/tests/e2e/quant_inference_perf_test.py where tolerances are defined per model family.
Marcus Lee (reviewer): CI perf job flaked once on blackwell-1; observed 7% regression on a microbench run. Did you root cause?

Ethan Rodriguez (author): Root cause was an L2 bank conflict introduced by a tiling change; adjusted tile shape heuristics when sm_version >= 95. Reran perf job and numbers are back within 1% of baseline.

release_notes: Performance: reduced median token latency on INT8 workloads by 12-20% and tail (p99) by 18-35% depending on model and sequence length. Added new experimental feature flag runtime.quant.experimental_fused_kernels. Stability: numeric tolerance tables added for FP8/INT8; no user-facing API changes.
notes_for_ops: Rollout behind feature flag. Start with canary traffic on dedicated-ns 'quant-canary' with profiling enabled. Monitor perf-ci dashboards and numeric-regression alerts. If p99 latency increases or numeric regressions exceed thresholds, disable flag and rollback.
notes: This PR combines low-level kernel work with runtime scheduler changes; reviewers should validate both microbenchmarks and end-to-end behavior on representative workloads.
